# 12. Cooperative Behaviors

## 12.1 C-ACC Group Protocol

Cooperative Adaptive Cruise Control (C-ACC) extends conventional ACC with inter-vehicle coordination. The C-ACC Group Protocol specifies how a set of vehicles forms an explicit coordinated group, maintains synchronized gap targets, hands off leadership, and dissolves.

### 12.1.1 State Machine

Every C-ACC Group passes through the following states:

```text
       +-------+                 +---------+
  ---->| IDLE  |---- propose --->| FORMING |
       +-------+                 +---------+
                                      |
                       (all members confirm, leader elected)
                                      v
                                 +---------+
                                 | STABLE  |
                                 +---------+
                                  |       ^
                                  |       |
                  (leader change) |       | (handoff complete)
                                  v       |
                                 +---------+
                                 | HANDOFF |
                                 +---------+
                                      |
                    (driver release, gap breach,
                     attestation loss, or off-ramp)
                                      v
                                 +-----------+
                                 | DISSOLVING|
                                 +-----------+
                                      |
                                      v
                                   IDLE
```

### 12.1.2 Formation

A C-ACC Group is formed by proposal. Any vehicle in an IDLE state MAY transmit a PLATOON_FORM Intent addressed to a specific peer (by pseudonym cert ID) or to the neighborhood. Peers that receive the proposal and wish to join transmit their own PLATOON_FORM Intent within a 2-second window. Once all proposed members have confirmed, one of them generates a group UUID and transmits the first GroupState with mode=FORMING; the group transitions to STABLE once all members have acknowledged the GroupState and the leader has observed stable gap-keeping for at least 5 seconds.

### 12.1.3 Driver Authorization

No vehicle shall transition from IDLE to FORMING on an inbound proposal without the driver’s explicit authorization for that specific proposal. The authorization MUST be revocable at any instant through a standard mechanism on the vehicle’s HMI; revocation immediately transitions the group to DISSOLVING from that vehicle’s perspective, and that vehicle’s C-ACC function reverts to conventional ACC with the production gap setting.

### 12.1.4 Leader Election and Handoff

The initial leader of a group is the proposer. Leadership MAY transfer on the following triggers: the leader’s intent to leave the group, detection of leader misbehavior by consensus of the remaining members, or an explicit handoff request from the leader. Handoff uses a two-phase commit: the outgoing leader nominates a successor in a GroupState with mode=HANDOFF; the successor accepts with its own GroupState carrying an incremented epoch and the new leader cert ID; once all non-leader members have acknowledged, the group returns to STABLE.

### 12.1.5 Dissolution

A group dissolves when any of the following occur: all but one member have left; the leader loses attestation or its certificate is revoked; a gap target is violated for more than 3 seconds by any member; or an explicit dissolve is transmitted by the leader. On entry to DISSOLVING, all members revert immediately to local ADAS without cooperative inputs. The group epoch is retired and the group UUID MUST NOT be reused.

### 12.1.6 Safety Envelopes

Within STABLE, the group’s gap target MUST be no shorter than 0.8 seconds on limited-access roads, no shorter than 1.2 seconds on arterial roads, and MUST widen automatically as a function of road class, weather (via local sensors), speed, and the weakest attestation state among group members. A group whose weakest member has lost attestation MUST widen to the conventional ACC production gap within 2 seconds and MUST begin a HANDOFF or DISSOLVING transition as appropriate.

## 12.2 Slipstream Mode (Optional Extension)

Slipstream Mode is an optional application-layer overlay on top of the C-ACC Group Protocol. It is the Strynex-branded extension referenced in §1.2 and is not required for base O-CPS conformance. This section specifies it because public interoperability requires a common definition.

### 12.2.1 Functional Additions

- Greenwave integration: consumes SPaT (SAE J2735) messages from intersection RSUs and optimizes the group’s approach speed to arrive in the green phase, subject to driver override and posted limits.
- Convoy voice channel: a group-scoped push-to-talk or VOX voice channel using the local sidelink mesh as the primary transport, with cellular fallback. Voice traffic is out-of-band with respect to the safety message classes and MUST NOT contend with PerceptionSummary or Intent for radio resources.
- Role-based cooperative responsibilities: lead-car responsibilities (setting group speed, sharing enhanced perception horizon) and follower responsibilities (maintaining gap, confirming intents).

### 12.2.2 Transport Preference Order

Slipstream Mode transports, in priority order, are:

- C-V2X PC5 sidelink or ITS-G5 direct (as for base O-CPS safety messages).
- Wi-Fi Aware / 802.11bd direct mesh (for voice and non-safety traffic only).
- Cellular relay via the group leader’s uplink (fallback for voice only; MUST NOT be used for any safety message class).

## 12.3 Intersection Assist (Optional Extension)

Intersection Assist consumes RSU-sourced MAP and SPaT messages (SAE J2735) together with local PerceptionSummary traffic to alert the driver to red-light runners, cross-traffic at blind intersections, and unprotected left-turn conflicts. It produces advisory output only and is always driver-mediated. Detailed specification is out of scope for v0.2 and is deferred to a forthcoming extension profile.
